discussion_comments.comment_body: AI Review: `createShellTools()` captures `engine.isEnabled()` before create/resume can report managed settings, and this event only invalidates `TerminalSandboxEngine` internals. If launch starts disabled and the session or runtime policy later turns sandboxing on, the existing handler still skips `wrapCommand()` and executes the raw command. Re-read enablement for each invocation (or rebuild the tools), and add an execution test covering a false-to-true transition.

AI Review: `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` may be locked on by the native `ChatAgentSandboxEnabled` policy, but the forwarder sends only its effective value and drops `policyValue`. With no separate Copilot managed-settings floor, a session `off` reaches this branch and is spread after root config in both sandbox consumers, disabling containment despite that policy. Carry the native policy floor/provenance into Agent Host, normalize or reject `off`, and disable the toggle while locked.

AI Review: `policy.allowBypass === true` means managed policy permits bypass, but this converts it into the affirmative host opt-in `allowUnsandboxedCommands: true`. Since these overrides are spread after root config, this can override an explicit or policy-controlled `false` and enable bypass in both SDK and custom-terminal paths. Managed `false` may force `false`; managed `true` should preserve or intersect with the root opt-in rather than force `true`.

AI Review: Live peer Copilot SDK sessions can share the same owner `configurationResource`, so each managed-settings callback writes this one map slot. A later weaker snapshot can replace a mandatory `{ enabled: true, allowBypass: false }` floor from a still-live sibling, after which all sibling SDK/custom-terminal checks read the weaker value. Store policy contributions per runtime, aggregate them deny-wins per owner, and remove each contribution when its runtime is disposed.

discussion_comments.comment_body: AI Review: The same running `toolCallId` can be confirmed again, and the reducer retains prior `_meta` when a later ready action omits it. After an allow-once sandbox escape sets this marker, a subsequent ordinary confirmation can remain tagged as a bypass; choosing Allow in this Session then disables sandboxing instead of adding the tool permission. Clear or explicitly stamp the bypass marker for every confirmation, and test bypass -> allow-once -> ordinary re-confirmation.

AI Review: This gallery request is still reachable when the effective chat.mcp.access value is none, including when policy-enforced. Selecting the MCP section can therefore issue a marketplace GET even though access-disabled UI is shown, and revocation leaves delayed or in-flight searches alive. Include effective access in snapshot/search eligibility and cancel delayedGallerySearch plus galleryCts when access becomes none; cover initial disabled visibility and revocation in tests.

Good catch, and still valid on the current code. Rather than set `followRedirects: 0` at every call site (easy to miss one), `NodeRequestService` now drops `Authorization`/`Cookie` whenever a followed redirect leaves the origin, so every token-bearing marketplace request is covered (e18b33bc229, with tests). The RFC 8693 exchange itself also sets `followRedirects: 0` since its body carries the subject token.

Fixed the same way on the GitHub `onDidChangeDefaultAccount` listener — the manifest is revoked (`update(null)`) before revalidation, so the old account's authorization can't leak into the new one on a transient failure.
